definition: In historical psychology, medium trance refers to a trance state associated with mediumship in which a person may seem to speak or act from another source. It can range from partial states, where the ordinary self still takes part, to more complete trances marked by altered speech or manner and little or no memory afterward; its early stages were described as resembling hypnotic suggestion and shaped by expectation.
